Week 87 Appendix: A Week That Nearly Balanced

Courts blocked the president repeatedly while he threatened electoral refusal, press bans, and coerced loyalty payments in return.

This week combined an unusually dense set of judicial rebukes to executive overreach with equally dense evidence of executive lawlessness, informational manipulation, and normalization of extremist rhetoric within the governing party. The Supreme Court repeatedly blocked Trump administration actions (mail-ballot restrictions, Fed governor removal, birthright citizenship rules, gerrymandered maps), and lower courts checked Kennedy Center demolition threats and DHS speech-suppression tactics — signaling institutional resilience. Simultaneously, Trump banned major news outlets from the White House, threatened to withhold disaster aid and Kennedy Center funds based on political loyalty, and Republican leadership (Speaker Johnson) openly floated refusing to seat a Democratic majority after the midterms. DHS was shown fabricating voter-fraud data at massive scale. AI governance emerged as a rare bipartisan-adjacent flashpoint, with industry leaders calling for a slowdown while Trump dismissed safety concerns as a partisan hoax. Republican electoral anxiety and intra-party fracture over racist rhetoric and immigration enforcement were also prominent.
